hook.text: Russia was one of the world's largest empires. In 1917, a revolutionary party seized its capital in hours. But taking control of Russia itself was a much longer struggle.

crisis.text: World War One drained the empire. Millions died, and bread ran short.

tsar.text: In February 1917, strikes and mutinies in Petrograd forced Nicholas the Second to abdicate. A Provisional Government took over.

lenin.text: It kept fighting the war. Lenin's Bolsheviks promised peace, land, and bread, and workers and soldiers listened.

october.text: On October twenty-fifth, by the old Russian calendar, Bolsheviks seized Petrograd's key points and toppled the Provisional Government. November seventh, in the Gregorian calendar.

civil_war.text: But holding the capital was not holding Russia. Civil war split the empire between Reds and Whites.

consolidation.text: By 1922, through war and tight centralised control, the Bolsheviks had won.

end.text: The capital fell in hours. Consolidating power took years.
